BAR for rust-2b (written 2026-10-03 before any run). This is a BAR: it can come out against Rust, for Rust, or as a tie. Expected values are written below so a surprise is visible.

 RULE A AND HOSTS (verifier pass 2026-10-03). LOG.md 2026-09-12 14:16Z ruled box2 timing INADMISSIBLE (Rule A: timing numbers only on box1) and state/BOXES.md still reads box1 "NO timing numbers until CPUQuota/thermal checked" and box2 "NO timing numbers (Rule A)"; box3 is the same CPU as box2. The ONLY labelled host is box1; box2 and box3 are reported with no label ("informal per Rule A"). Before registration the registrar checks box1 CPUQuota and thermal state while idle, records the dated result, and gets BOXES.md updated (spot read only, not the check: 2026-10-04 00:12Z cm-tick CPUQuotaPerSecUSec=infinity, thermal zones 25 to 30 C, load 1.68 from other jobs). A written Fable or Justin ruling admitting box2 may reinstate it as a labelled host by amend-bar before start only; the two-host rules are kept in brackets for that case.

ANSWERS: FRAMEWORK (a Rust training framework against PyTorch). It does not answer LANGUAGE (no C arm) or KERNELS (each framework brings its own kernels).
LABEL ON THE RESULT: "framework, not language".
SCALE LINE: "Scale: 1 to 5 million parameters, CPU, 200 steps. GPU training and 135M to 360M models are untested and do not follow."

QUESTION. On the same small character transformer, same initial weights and same batches, does Burn (CPU Flex backend) train at a higher, equal or lower speed than PyTorch on an old laptop CPU, and does it reach the same loss?

WHAT IS COMPARED.
 B  Burn, CPU "Flex" backend with autodiff. Version DECIDED by a dated check (crates.io index read 2026-10-04 00:17Z): burn 0.21.0 is published and not yanked, has the feature `flex`, and depends on burn-flex 0.21.0 (also published, not yanked). Burn 0.21.0 with features flex and autodiff is the arm; the 0.22.0 pre-releases (latest 0.22.0-pre.4) are not used. Features, rustc and RUSTFLAGS recorded and frozen before the initial timing (Cargo.lock sha256 recorded). PURE RUST: decided by `cargo tree --edges normal,build` and the build log before timing: any -sys crate, build.rs that invokes a C or C++ compiler, or runtime loading of a native library makes the label NOT PURE RUST, otherwise PURE RUST; the label is written in the result next to every number.
 T  PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu, fp32, same model written with torch.nn primitives, torch.set_num_threads(N), torch.set_num_interop_threads(1), OMP_NUM_THREADS=N, MKL_NUM_THREADS=N, no torch.compile, sdpa attention, torch.__config__.show() kept. NOT pure Rust.
 Extra, reported only: Candle (autodiff, CPU) if it builds with the same model in under half a day; labelled NOT PURE RUST (gemm crate is Rust, MKL off, version recorded).
Model (fixed now): byte-level decoder transformer, vocabulary 256, context 64, d_model 192, 4 layers, 6 heads, feed-forward 768 with GELU, pre-LayerNorm, learned position embeddings, tied output head, no dropout; NUMERIC OPTIONS (fixed now, identical in both arms): GELU is the exact erf form, 0.5 x (1 + erf(x / sqrt 2)), not the tanh approximation; LayerNorm epsilon 1e-5 with gain and bias, biased variance over d_model; every Linear (q, k, v, attention output, both feed-forward layers) has a bias, the tied head has none; attention scale 1/sqrt(32) (head size 192 / 6), causal mask applied before the softmax, softmax in fp32 over keys, no attention dropout; pre-LN residual blocks and one final LayerNorm before the head; loss = mean cross-entropy over all 16 x 64 next-byte positions; AdamW epsilon 1e-8, bias correction on, decoupled weight decay 0.01 applied to every parameter (p <- p x (1 - lr x wd) before the Adam step, torch semantics), no gradient clipping; fp32 throughout. The init file holds every parameter (token and position tables, LayerNorm gains 1 and biases 0 as the script writes them, all projections), so no initialiser runs in either arm. PRE-TIMING CHECK: one step from the same init and batch in B and T must agree to 1e-5 absolute on the loss and 1e-4 on every parameter; a disagreement is traced to a spec item above or to a Burn default that must be overridden before any timing, and a Burn behaviour that cannot be matched is written down (then LOSS DIVERGENT is the expected outcome and is not a Burn-quality finding); about 1.8 million parameters (the exact count is computed in both arms and must be equal, within 1 to 5 million). AdamW, lr 3e-4 constant, betas 0.9 and 0.999, weight decay 0.01, batch 16 sequences, 200 timed steps after 5 untimed warm-up steps (the warm-up steps are not counted in the 200 and do not change the data order of the 200). Data: one fixed benign public-domain text file of about 1 MB (path and sha256 recorded at build) and one batch-order index file (sha256) shared by both arms. Initial weights: written once by a one-off script into a flat fp32 file (sha256) read by both arms, so the initial loss is equal to 6 digits; dropout off so no RNG is used in the 200 steps.

METRICS. Steps per second (per-rep value = 200 / wall seconds of the 200 timed steps, in-process, after the warm-up); loss at step 200 (mean of the last 10 training-batch losses); peak PSS from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup (median of reps). Threads N=1 for labels; N=2 on box1 and box2 reported with no label. Statistic: median of 5 reps per arm per host (10 once on INCONCLUSIVE). Arm order rotated every rep.

LABELS (no gaps, no overlaps). r = B median steps/s divided by T median steps/s.
 Loss condition, applied before the speed labels: |loss_B(200) - loss_T(200)| <= 0.05 nats. If it fails the label is LOSS DIVERGENT: the speed labels below are INVALID for that host, the divergence is reported with the cause (different arithmetic, a Burn defect, a model mismatch), and no speed sentence is written.
 If the loss condition holds: BURN AHEAD: r > 1.10 and every B rep value above every T rep value. TIE: 0.90 <= r <= 1.10. BURN BEHIND: r < 0.90 and every T rep value above every B rep value. INCONCLUSIVE: r outside 0.90 to 1.10 with overlapping rep ranges; redone as 10; if still overlapping the label is TIE (NOT SEPARABLE).
 Overall = the box1 label (FRAMEWORK: BURN AHEAD, BURN BEHIND, or LEVEL for TIE and NOT SEPARABLE). If box1 is LOSS DIVERGENT, DID NOT RUN or INVALID there is no overall label (the reason is quoted) and none is built from box2 or box3. [Only if box2 is admitted by a recorded ruling and the bar amended before start: both AHEAD gives BURN AHEAD, both BEHIND gives BURN BEHIND, both TIE or NOT SEPARABLE gives LEVEL, and any other combination, including one host LOSS DIVERGENT or DID NOT RUN, gives FRAMEWORK: MIXED with both host results and reasons quoted.]
 Memory (reported, label by the same band on the PSS ratio): BURN LOWER if ratio < 0.90, TIE 0.90 to 1.10, BURN HIGHER above 1.10, with the same rep-range rule.

TRUST COLUMN. (1) Run-to-run equality: the final weights file hash of two runs of the same arm on the same host (reported, expected equal for B and for T at N=1). (2) Cross-host equality: final weights hash on box1 versus box2, reported for both arms; bit-equality is NOT required and is not argued (pinned exp/ln differ between frameworks). (3) Dependency count (Cargo.lock packages against pip packages and installed bytes). (4) PURE RUST yes or no for B.

EXPECTED (ESTIMATE, before any run). BURN BEHIND about 55 percent, TIE about 25 percent, BURN AHEAD about 20 percent at N=1 on box1, with the same expectation on box2 (reported, no label). Memory on box2 (limit 2.8 GB) is untested for Burn autodiff; ESTIMATE: parameters, Adam state and batch 16 x 64 activations fit in well under 1 GB; a kill by the limit is recorded as OOM, not dropped. Reason: public Rust-framework CPU reports run behind PyTorch (Candle 122 ms against PyTorch 14 ms on one encoder, REPORTED in PRIOR-ART.md section 2, single unreviewed issue, features cuda+cudnn+mkl so unclear if CPU), but this model is tiny and PyTorch dispatch overhead is large at 1.8 million parameters, so Burn could be level. LOSS DIVERGENT about 15 percent (a model-porting slip). Memory: BURN LOWER about 65 percent (no Python and no MKL runtime in the process); that would be a no-Python effect and the sentence says so.

INVALID (affected label gets no verdict, redo): host load 0.3 or more before or after; a kept rep with clock drop above 15 percent; model parameter counts differ; init file or batch-order hash differs between arms; threads not equal to N; the Burn arm cannot run on box1 (then it reads "B: DID NOT RUN, cause", no label; the same line is written for box2 and box3 and there it only affects their reported lines); a harness bug.

FIXED NOW (may not change after the initial timing run): the model, optimiser, data and batch-order files, steps, warm-up, bands, loss tolerance 0.05, labelled host box1 (box2 and box3 reported, Rule A), the numeric options and the pre-timing check, thread settings, memory limits (box1 4.5 GB, box2 and box3 2.8 GB, under systemd-run --user), the sentences. Recorded and frozen before the initial timing: framework versions and flags.

HOSTS. Labelled host: box1 (AVX2). Reported with no label (Rule A): box2 (no AVX2) and box3 (same CPU). box4 and box5: not run (no PyTorch). Penguin: builds only, no timing.

SENTENCES.
 "FRAMEWORK, not language (CPU, 1.8M-parameter byte transformer, 200 steps, N=1): Burn <Flex, pure Rust | Flex, not pure Rust> is <ahead of | level with | behind> PyTorch on <host>, steps/s ratio r=<x>, final loss <a> against <b>."
 Overall: "FRAMEWORK: <BURN AHEAD | BURN BEHIND | LEVEL | MIXED>. Scale: 1 to 5 million parameters on CPU only; GPU training and 135M to 360M models are untested."
 Loss: "LOSS DIVERGENT on <host> (<a> against <b>): no speed sentence is written."
 Memory: "FRAMEWORK (memory): Burn peak PSS is <lower than | level with | higher than> PyTorch on <host>, ratio <x>; <no-Python effect, not a Rust-language effect>."
title: rust-2b: Burn (CPU Flex) vs PyTorch training a 1.8M-parameter byte transformer, 200 steps (FRAMEWORK)

 A1 PIN, recorded and frozen before the initial timing. Burn 0.21.0 with features flex and autodiff: burn = "=0.21.0", default-features = false, features = ["flex", "autodiff"], and, as the same framework as shipped, burn-flex = "=0.21.0" with default-features = false and features = ["std", "simd", "rayon"], which are burn-flex's own default features. Reason: burn's flex feature alone leaves those three off (checked with cargo tree -e features), so the build would have no thread pool, no SIMD and no std in the backend, N=2 would not be honoured, and the label sentence "Burn Flex" would not describe the framework as shipped; features flex and autodiff are both on. rayon = "=1.12.0" as a direct dependency to set and read the thread pool.
